changes.text: 赵王召见相如，问他：秦王要用十五座城换我的璧，可以给吗？相如答：秦强而赵弱，不能不答应；秦以城求璧而赵不许，理亏在赵；赵给了璧而秦不给城，理亏在秦。「均之二策，甯許以負秦曲」——两相比较，宁可答应，让理亏落到秦国头上。赵王问谁可以出使，相如自请奉璧前往：城归赵，璧就留在秦；城不归赵，「臣請完璧歸趙」。赵王于是派相如奉璧西入秦国。

The king summoned Lin Xiangru and asked him: the king of Qin wants to trade fifteen cities for my jade; may I give it? Lin Xiangru answered that Qin was strong and Zhao weak, so Zhao could not refuse. If Qin offers cities for the jade and Zhao refuses, the wrong is Zhao's; if Zhao hands over the jade and Qin refuses the cities, the wrong is Qin's. Weighing the two courses together, it is better to agree and leave Qin carrying the blame. When the king asked who could go as envoy, Lin Xiangru offered to carry the jade himself: if the cities came to Zhao, the jade would stay in Qin; if they did not, he would bring the jade back to Zhao intact. So the king sent Lin Xiangru west into Qin with the jade.

到了秦廷，秦王在章台接见相如，接过璧大喜，传给身边的美人和侍从看，左右都高呼万岁。相如看出秦王无意偿城，上前说璧有小毛病要指给秦王看，拿到璧便退立倚柱，怒发上冲冠，当面斥责秦王，放话：大王若一定要逼我，「臣頭今與璧倶碎於柱矣」；直到此时才「持其璧睨柱，欲以撃柱」。秦王怕他砸碎，连忙道歉，召来主管官员查看地图，指着说从这里过去的十五座城给赵。相如判断这不过是做样子，城根本拿不到，于是说和氏璧是天下共传之宝，赵王送来前斋戒五日，秦王也该斋戒五日，设九宾于廷，他才敢献璧。秦王答应了，把他安置在广成传舍。相如断定秦王即便斋戒也一定违约，就让随从穿上粗布衣，把璧揣在怀里，从小路逃走，送回赵国。等再次上廷，他把话摊开：秦自缪公以来二十多位国君，没有一位说话算数；璧已送回赵国，「臣知欺大王之罪當誅，臣請就湯鑊」。秦王与群臣相视而嘻，左右有人要把他拉下去，秦王最终说，杀了相如也得不到璧，反而断了秦赵之好，不如以礼相待送他回去，「卒廷見相如，畢禮而歸之」。相如回国后，赵王认为他是贤大夫，出使不辱于诸侯，拜他为上大夫；而秦终究没有把城给赵，赵也始终没有把璧给秦。

At the Qin court the king received Lin Xiangru in the Zhang Terrace, was delighted with the jade, and passed it around to his ladies and attendants, who all cried long life to him. Lin Xiangru saw he had no intention of paying. He said the gem had a small flaw he would point out, took it back and stood against a pillar, his hair bristling with anger, and denounced the king, warning that if the king insisted on pressing him, his head and the jade would be smashed together against the pillar. Only then did he stand holding the jade with his eyes on the pillar, ready to bring it down. The alarmed king apologised, summoned the officials concerned to consult the map and pointed out fifteen cities for Zhao. Lin Xiangru judged this mere show. The Heshi jade was a treasure the whole world talked of, he said; the king of Zhao had fasted five days before sending it, and the king of Qin should fast five days and hold the nine-fold ceremony at court before he would dare present it. The king agreed and lodged him at the Guangcheng hostel. Sure that the king would break his word even after fasting, Lin Xiangru had a follower put on coarse clothes, hide the jade in his robe and take it home to Zhao by back roads. At the next audience he laid it out: in more than twenty reigns since Duke Mu, Qin had never kept a firm agreement; the jade was already back in Zhao; he knew that deceiving the king was a crime deserving death, and he asked to be sent to the cauldron. The king and his ministers looked at one another and laughed wryly. Some attendants moved to drag him out, but the king reasoned that killing him would not bring back the jade and would end good relations with Zhao. In the end he received Lin Xiangru at court with full ceremony and sent him home. Once Lin Xiangru was back, the king of Zhao, judging him a worthy grandee who had not disgraced Zhao among the states, made him shangdafu. In the end Qin never handed the cities to Zhao, and Zhao never gave Qin the jade.

此后秦国伐赵，攻下石城；第二年又攻赵，杀了二万人。秦王派使者告诉赵王，想在西河外的渑池与他相会修好。赵王畏秦，不想去；廉颇、蔺相如商议说：「王不行，示趙弱且怯也。」赵王于是赴会，相如随行。廉颇送王到边境，与赵王诀别时约定：算上路程和会面的礼节，往返不超过三十日；三十日不回，就请立太子为王，断掉秦国的念想。赵王答应了。到了渑池，秦王酒酣，请赵王鼓瑟，赵王鼓了，秦御史上前记下「某年月日，秦王與趙王會飲，令趙王鼓瑟」。相如上前，请秦王击缻以相娱乐，秦王发怒，不答应；相如捧缻上前，跪着请求，秦王仍不肯击。相如说：「五歩之内，相如請得以頸血濺大王矣！」秦王左右要拿刀杀相如，「相如張目叱之，左右皆靡」。秦王不高兴，只好击了一下缻，相如回头召赵御史记下：某年某月某日，秦王为赵王击缻。秦国群臣说，请以赵国十五座城为秦王祝寿；相如也说：「請以秦之咸陽爲趙王壽。」秦王直到酒宴结束，「終不能加勝於趙」；赵国也「盛設兵以待秦」，秦不敢动。

After this Qin attacked Zhao and took Shicheng; the following year it attacked again and killed twenty thousand men. The king of Qin sent an envoy proposing a friendly meeting with the king of Zhao at Mianchi, beyond the Western River. The king of Zhao, afraid of Qin, wanted not to go, but Lian Po and Lin Xiangru advised that if the king stayed away it would show Zhao as weak and timid. So the king went, with Lin Xiangru in attendance. Lian Po escorted the king to the border and, taking leave, made an arrangement: allow for the road and the formalities of the meeting, and the round trip should take no more than thirty days; if the king was not back in thirty days, let the crown prince be set up as king, to cut off Qin's hopes. The king agreed. At Mianchi, when the wine was flowing, the king of Qin asked the king of Zhao to play the se, and he did; a Qin scribe stepped forward and recorded that on such a day the king of Qin, drinking with the king of Zhao, had ordered the king of Zhao to play the se. Lin Xiangru then came forward and asked the king of Qin to strike an earthen pot for their mutual entertainment. The king of Qin angrily refused. Lin Xiangru brought the pot forward, knelt and pressed him; still the king would not strike it. Lin Xiangru said that within five paces he could spatter the king with the blood from his own neck. The king's attendants moved to cut him down, but Lin Xiangru glared and shouted at them, and they all fell back. Displeased, the king of Qin struck the pot once, and Lin Xiangru turned and called the Zhao scribe to record that on such a day the king of Qin had struck the pot for the king of Zhao. Qin's ministers asked for fifteen cities of Zhao as a toast to the king of Qin's long life; Lin Xiangru asked in return for Qin's Xianyang as a toast to the king of Zhao's long life. To the end of the banquet the king of Qin could not gain the upper hand over Zhao; Zhao, for its part, had massed its forces to meet Qin, and Qin dared not move.
值得一提的是廉颇的委屈。他的功劳是攻城野战，相如的功劳在秦廷与渑池；作者认为，两种功劳形态不同，本不好用同一把尺子量。他说相如「素賤人」、羞于居下，一种解释是，他不服的不只是排序，还有出身。还有一种解释是，廉颇计较的不是功劳有无，而是功劳能否被看见——战场胜负可以点数，口舌上的成败要靠人转述。

Lian Po's grievance deserves a moment first. His merit was won storming cities; Lin Xiangru's, at the Qin court and at Mianchi. In the author's view, the two kinds of credit have different shapes and are not easily measured with one ruler. He jibed that Lin Xiangru had always been a man of low station and that he was ashamed to rank beneath him; one reading is that what rankled was not only the ordering but the birth behind it. Another reading is that what Lian Po cared about was not whether merit existed but whether it could be seen: a battlefield result can be counted off, whereas success with words depends on someone else retelling it.
同一篇列传里，认错的动作出现过两次。早年缪贤有罪，相如给他出的主意是「肉袒伏斧質請罪」；后来廉颇上门，做的是「肉袒負荊」。两者都是脱去上衣、把身体交出去的姿势。不能断言廉颇知道前一桩事或受其影响（作者提示，非原文所述）。另外，相如答赵王时的那段权衡用的是另一套语言：先说清「曲在趙」还是「曲在秦」，把理亏的一方安排到对方。太史公的评语是「退而讓頗，名重太山」——退让，反而把名望抬到了泰山那么高。

Within the same biography the gesture of admitting fault appears twice. Lin Xiangru's advice to Miao Xian was to strip and lie on the block to ask pardon; when Lian Po came to the gate, he came stripped to the waist with thorns on his back. Both are postures of baring the body and handing it over. One cannot say that Lian Po knew of the earlier case or was influenced by it; the parallel is the author's observation, not something the text states. The weighing Lin Xiangru offered the king when he answered him uses a different grammar: first settle where the wrong will lie, with Zhao or with Qin, and arrange for it to fall on the other side. The Grand Historian's verdict: he stepped back and yielded to Lian Po, and his name came to weigh as much as Mount Tai.
需要说明的不确定性：本文所据材料只有司马迁《廉颇蔺相如列传》一篇，其中的对话是史书的记述，未必是逐字实录；负荆请罪的细节——袒身、背荆条、由宾客引见——在本篇的证据中没有其他材料可以核对。文中对原文未写的人物心理所作的推断，作者尽量以“一种解释是”“作者认为”标明为解释。年份只用原文的「趙惠文王時」这类说法，不换算公元年。

The uncertainty to flag: the only material this piece draws on is Sima Qian's biography of Lian Po and Lin Xiangru. The speeches there are a historian's record and need not be verbatim transcripts, and the details of the thorn apology - the bared body, the bundle of thorns, the arrival by way of guests - cannot be checked against any other material in this piece's evidence. Where the piece infers a figure's inner thoughts beyond what the original text says, the author tries to mark such claims as one reading or as the author's inference. Dates stay in the source's own terms, such as in the time of King Huiwen of Zhao, rather than being converted into years before the common era.
虚构一个场景：一家公司的技术团队里，老工程师带了七八年核心系统，新来的同事凭几次故障处置和几场汇报被提拔到他上面。老工程师在周会上说，他不过会讲话。新同事听到风声，开会从不与他争，排期上也让。组里年轻人替新同事不平，觉得他太软。这个局面和朝堂上那两位的区别只在道具：没有马车，只有会议纪要。

Take an invented scene. On a company's engineering team, the veteran who has kept the core system alive for seven or eight years watches a newcomer promoted above him on the strength of a few incident recoveries and a handful of status reviews. At the weekly meeting the old engineer mutters that his rival is nothing but a talker. The newcomer hears about it and never argues with him, conceding even on scheduling. The younger members of the team feel he is being far too soft. The only difference from that ancient court is the furniture: no carriages, only meeting minutes.
